text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD p99 streaming latency spike detected in eu-west-2 across multiple clusters. metric: https://grafana.internal/redwood/streams?panelId=9 alert: p99 > 1.2s for 5m, streaming stalls observed. auto-page to eng-oncall.
Sam (eng-oncall): saw it, joining. any customer-facing impact yet?
Lina (support): CS reports 3 customers on premium experiencing timeouts for long-polling streams. ticket numbers: #C-4482, #C-4485.
Javier (netops): eyeballing VPC egress metrics — NAT SNAT port exhaustion chatter and increased retransmits on cross-zone paths.
Priya (prod-sre): adding logs: streaming tail p95 jumped from 120ms -> 580ms, p99 to 1.3s. tail stalls correlate with TLS handshake retries.
Sam (eng-oncall): ok can we confirm DNS/backoff? who runs the egress path?
Javier (netops): running traceroutes, seeing asymmetric path via nat-gw-eu-03 and eu-01 intermittently. DNS lookup latencies spiking ~300-600ms with intermittent SERVFAILs.
Priya (prod-sre): reproduction: local curl to streaming endpoint returns handshake delays. captured sample: "TLS handshake: SYN->SYN/ACK 120ms, TLS client hello -> server hello 400ms".
Sam (eng-oncall): start mitigations: 1) reroute subset of traffic away from nat-gw-eu-03 2) increase SNAT ephemeral port pool 3) reduce DNS TTL for streaming endpoints to 30s for quicker failover. anyone object?
Javier (netops): on it. pushing policy to steer lb-weights away from eu-03 for canary (10% -> 0%) and start draining. applying iptables tweak on NAT hosts to extend port range.
Lina (support): notifying affected customers: message draft ready, need approval: "We're investigating elevated streaming latency in EU, working on mitigation, will update in 30m."
Alex-CS: approve draft. flagging premium customers and offering rollback windows.
Priya (prod-sre): collecting traces: attaching sample RPC flow: 
```
trace-id: a1b2c3
event1: client send
event2: gateway accept
event3: nat handshake retry
event4: server response delayed
```
These align with SNAT port churn and TCP retransmit bursts.
Javier (netops): running tcpdump on nat-gw-eu-03 for 60s: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 port 443 -w /tmp/eu03.pcap` capturing retransmit pairs. sending to /eng/infra for deeper net analysis.
Sam (eng-oncall): good. also enable streaming debug sampling on 1% of requests to capture KV cache hits/misses and exact latencies.
Priya (prod-sre): temporary config change rolling: set streaming keepalive to 15s (was 60s) to surface dead connections faster. will monitor for regression.
Javier (netops): applied SNAT range increase on nat-gw-eu-03 and eu-01: 32768-61000 -> 32768-65535. watch for immediate improvement.
Sam (eng-oncall): any improvement metrics?
Priya (prod-sre): preliminary: p95 down from 580ms -> 260ms within 6m of SNAT bump for flows routed off eu-03. p99 still ~700ms for some flows pinned to eu-03.
Javier (netops): draining completed. LB now routes >95% away from eu-03. eu-03 still has a queue backpressure on conntrack entries, cleaning up via conntrack -L and increase timeout.
Lina (support): customer update: sent initial note and escalated tickets. customers acknowledged and asked for ETA.
Alex-CS: customers want SLA credit estimate. Lina, collect session ids and impacted windows.
Priya (prod-sre): running post-mitigation healthcheck: `curl -v https://streams.eu-west-2.redwood.ai/health` shows 200 with <100ms for canary.
Sam (eng-oncall): next steps: 1) keep eu-03 drained for 30m 2) full NAT host postmortem if conntrack thrash reappears 3) run interzone path MTU/checksum tests 4) coordinate with cloud provider if retransmits persist.
Javier (netops): opened infra ticket INF-7726 to rotate NAT hosts and schedule kernel conntrack param changes (nf_conntrack_max bump). linking to thread.
Priya (prod-sre): add regression alert to catch TLS handshake spike pattern (pattern: repeated SYN retransmit followed by delayed TLS server hello) and tie to streaming SLOs.
Sam (eng-oncall): leaving a handoff: I'm paging oncall rotation in 30m. If p99>1s or >3 customers impacted escalate to SEV-2.
Lina (support): leaving shift at 20:00 UTC, handing to @Alex-CS for follow-ups.
Alex-CS: got it, will own customer comms and SLA calcs.
Priya (prod-sre): notes for postmortem (to add): root cause hypotheses: 1) NAT ephemeral exhaustion + conntrack backpressure 2) intermittent DNS resolver flapping causing cross-zone reroutes 3) transient provider route flap causing handshake delays. evidence: SNAT port churn logs, DNS SERVFAIL spikes, traceroute asymmetry.
Sam (eng-oncall): good list. Actions captured in a quick checklist: `- drain eu-03, - increase SNAT, - bump conntrack, - add TLS-spike alert, - customer comms`.
incident-bot: incident status updated -> mitigation in progress. severity: SEV-3 (customer impact, partial), updated at 1767774820.
Priya (prod-sre): final note before handoff: keep monitoring streaming tail stalls and p99 for next 60m; if we see new stalls open immediate pager for SEV-2.
Alex-CS: will update customers in 30m with mitigation summary and next steps. posting tickets to billing for SLA review. :thumbsup:
Sam (eng-oncall): handing off to Alex-CS and Javier for overnight monitoring. I remain on rotation but will sleep if no pager in 60m :sleeping: .
Javier (netops): will keep tcpdump rolling and watch conntrack metrics. ping me if you need wire captures.
Lina (support): thanks team, closing out support side for now.
